lacuna.name: engine-kv-capacity-preemption-coupling
lacuna.repo_anchor: plan/0005-format-interop/README.md carries the coupling implicitly in three places that never name it: the Operator target section ("Both-card serving runs over the NVLink bridge ... FP8 ~27 GB weights -> ~14 GB/card with generous KV; W4A16 ~14 GB"), stage 7 ("FP8 KV: recast to fp16 KV at 2x memory (faithful, simple) or int8 KV (measured against fp16-KV quality); the serving config records which the checkpoint requires" - the 2x-capacity clause without the preemption consequence), and stage 13 ("the operator's Qwen3-class ~27B checkpoint across both GPUs, tokens/s committed with the serving configuration"). MEMORY.md 2026-09-07 (serving baseline framing) makes tokens/s the committed quantity without an overflow-behavior clause. Measured anchors this item builds on: plan/0007-d256-bridge/README.md 27B engine gate (2026-09-06, ALL 14 GATES PASS, PPL 2k = 6.7761, clean 512-token long decode to ctx 32768, MML 40960) and plan/0004-gap-closure (NVLink cross-GPU K-shard 43.7 GB/s). Hardware per MEMORY 2026-08-27: 2x Quadro RTX 6000 (TU102, 24 GB, PCIe 3.0 host, NVLink bridge), clocks locked 1455 MHz.
lacuna.current_status: As of 2026-09-07 every link of the capacity-preemption chain is individually documented upstream, but the chain itself is designed nowhere. (1) The failure chain in the field: vLLM #47549 (opened 2026-07-03 by ptempier, still open, no maintainer response, bug label only): an 18x Quadro RTX 8000 (SM7.5, 48 GB) fleet serving cyankiwi/MiniMax-M2.7-AWQ-4bit with RooCode agentic sessions at 18-24K contexts; v0.24.0 removed FlashInfer from the SM7.5 candidate list (side effect of backend-selection refactoring around the FLASHINFER_CUTLASS NVFP4 PR #46492, undocumented in release notes), the SM7.5 candidate list shrank from ['FLASHINFER','TRITON_ATTN'] to ['TRITON_ATTN'], requested fp8 KV raises 'FP8 KV cache is not supported by the Triton attention backend' at startup, forced fp16 fallback halves KV capacity 287,744 -> ~143,000 tokens, the scheduler preempts 'more aggressively at longer contexts', and decode at ~22K ctx collapses from ~5-11 tok/s to ~0.8-1.1 tok/s (5-10x); sole workaround is pinning vllm-openai:v0.23.0. (2) Preemption mode semantics: vLLM V1 default is RECOMPUTE rather than SWAP (docs v0.18.1 Optimization and Tuning); SWAP is V0-only - #18115 established that any non-default --preemption-mode value forces a V0 fallback, and V0 has since been removed from current releases, so swap is unreachable on any 2026 stack; the V1 metrics design doc confirms the swap-era vllm:num_requests_swapped metric is deprecated legacy for 'a swapped preemption mode that is no longer relevant in v1', with preemption now surfacing as a PREEMPTED engine-core event folded into inter-token/decode/inference interval accounting, alongside vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc (gauge) and vllm:cache_config_info (config labels). (3) KV compression state: TurboQuant (Google Research + NYU, arXiv 2504.19874, ICLR 2026, OpenReview tO3ASKZlok) delivers training-free near-lossless 3-bit and 4-bit online KV quantization (~4-5x memory reduction at the ~3.5-bit point per the paper); it is exposed in vLLM as kv-cache-dtype presets turboquant_3bit_nc / turboquant_4bit_nc / turboquant_k8v4, but the dtype path is backend-coupled and broken (#40094, 2026-04-17, L4, TRITON_ATTN and FLASH_ATTN both reject it) and gated under speculation: #40831 (2026-04-24, RTX 3090, Qwen3.6-27B hybrid GDN, all three TurboQuant presets x MTP at n=1 and n=3 produce degenerate token loops while TurboQuant alone passes all 7 verify checks including needle recall to 90K; fp8_e5m2 + MTP passes; hypothesis is the MTP draft head attending over the quantized cache silently accepting looping drafts; closed via out-of-tree genesis-vllm-patches P64-P69, not upstream; removing spec decode costs ~85 -> ~40 TPS on their bench) and its 2026 recurrence #53180 (opened 2026-08-21, v0.27.1 stock image, 2x RTX 4090 TP=2, cyankiwi/Qwen3.8-27B-AWQ-INT4: turboquant_k8v4 + MTP-3 intermittently and silently emits repetition walls - 4-gram repetition ratio 0.92-0.96 - with /health green, no log warnings, plausible acceptance metrics 0.34-0.38 vs 0.79 on fp8+MTP; config matrix: k8v4 alone PASS (multi-day soak), fp8+MTP PASS 17/17 gates, k8v4+MTP FAIL, k8v4+MTP+PR #51812 overlay still FAIL; caught only by a fixed-prompt temp-0 canary; open, no comments). This directly indicts the weicj/vLLM-2080Ti-Definitive flagship route (Qwen3.6-27B + TurboQuant K8V4 KV + MTP3): the combo is now field-proven fragile on the exact model class. (4) Hybrid-model state management: hybrid GDN/Mamba models are first-class in V1 (PyTorch blog 2025-11-05: unified allocator over KV and state pools, page-size alignment between attention blocks and Mamba pages, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE CUDA graphs; Mamba state is a large fixed per-sequence tensor, 2.57 MiB for Nemotron-Nano-12B-v2, updated in place), but the hybrid tail is thin: Mamba-2 prefix caching is experimental (#26201), Mamba prefix caching x MTP was never tested (#39809), external KV offload does not work out of the box for mamba hybrids like Qwen3.5 (#38230), and the scheduler caps concurrent Mamba sequences precisely because preempting them forces full state recompute. (5) MoE reference geometry verified: Qwen3-30B-A3B config.json = 48 layers, 32 Q / 4 KV heads, head_dim 128, 128 experts - 96 KiB/token fp16 KV (corroborated independently by vast.ai docs: '~188 GB KV for 200K context'), max context 32,768 native (1M via the 2507 sparse-attention config_1m.json).
lacuna.sm75_viability: Everything needed runs on this host today except the broken upstream TurboQuant dtype path; the deliverable is arithmetic plus a load-time assertion, not a kernel. ENVELOPE TABLE (computed from verified geometry; 1 GiB = 2^30 B; KV budget on 2x24 GB after ~14-15 GB W4A16 weights + ~2-3 GB overhead = 26-30 GiB aggregate, TP=2 shards the 4 KV heads 2+2 per card). Model A: Qwen3.6-27B hybrid (64 layers = 48 GDN + 16 full-attention; full-attn KV = 16 x 4 heads x head_dim 256 x 2(K,V) = 32,768 elements/token; GDN layers contribute zero per-token KV but 144 MiB/seq fixed fp32 state = 48 layers x 48 v-heads x 128 x 128 x 4 B, halvable to 72 MiB if an fp16 state path lands): per-token KV and tokens/GiB - fp16: 64 KiB, 16,384/GiB; int8 or fp8(emulated): 32 KiB, 32,768/GiB; TurboQuant K8V4: 24 KiB, 43,691/GiB (2.67x); 4-bit: 16 KiB, 65,536/GiB (4x); 3-bit: 12 KiB, 87,381/GiB (5.33x). Capacity on 26-30 GiB: fp16 426-492K tokens; int8/fp8 852-983K; K8V4 1.14-1.31M; 4-bit 1.70-1.97M; 3-bit 2.27-2.62M. Single-request context cost: 22K-class (22,528 tok) = 1.375 GiB fp16 / 0.69 int8 / 0.52 K8V4 / 0.34 4-bit; native 256K = 16 / 8 / 6 / 4 GiB. Model B: Qwen3-30B-A3B-class MoE (48 full-attn layers x 4 KV heads x 128, no recurrent state): fp16 96 KiB/token, 10,923/GiB; int8/fp8 48 KiB, 21,845/GiB; K8V4 36 KiB, 29,127/GiB; 4-bit 24 KiB, 43,691/GiB. Capacity on 26-30 GiB: fp16 284-328K; int8 568-655K; K8V4 757-874K tokens. Context cost: 22K = 2.06 GiB fp16 / 1.03 int8; 256K = 24 GiB fp16 (80-92% of the whole budget - native 256K on the MoE realistically requires int8 KV: 12 GiB) - the hybrid's 8x per-token advantage over this class is the structural reason the 27B is the primary. Reference C, the #47549 fleet class (dense 64-layer, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128): 256 KiB/token fp16, 4,096/GiB; their field numbers (fp8 287,744 tokens -> fp16 ~143,000 on the same hardware) are the empirical proof of the 2x row. Concurrency coupling on Model A: tokens are not the only axis - the GDN state prices every admitted sequence at 144 MiB flat (60 seqs = 8.4 GiB, 100 = 14.1, 150 = 21.1), so admission caps at roughly 100-180 sequences even when token capacity looks plentiful, and V1's scheduler already caps Mamba concurrency for exactly this reason. TurboQuant/MTP gate: per #40831/#53180, K8V4 and 3/4-bit KV are only valid WITHOUT MTP on this model class; fp8_e5m2 + MTP is the verified-passing compressed combination - but fp8 KV on sm75 itself rides only the FlashInfer software-conversion path (<= v0.23.0 or the fork), so the realistic sm75 arms are fp16+MTP3 (capacity-poor, 426-492K tokens), int8+MTP (if int8 KV passes the same interaction probe - untested under spec decode, gate it), or K8V4 without MTP (1.14-1.31M tokens at ~40 tok/s-class single-stream instead of ~85). PREEMPTION-MODE DECISION for 2x24 GB Turing (NVLink peer access vs host swap): (a) RECOMPUTE is the only reachable mode on any current stack - V1 hard-defaults to it, SWAP was V0-only (#18115) and V0 is gone from 2026 releases; on the fork's retained v0.21.0-class engine the same holds. (b) Host swap would be the wrong trade here even if it existed: a 22K fp16 KV eviction is a ~2.7 GiB round trip over PCIe 3.0 x16 (~12-13 GB/s effective per direction on this host's TU102 [uncertain: host_swap_effective_bandwidth]) = ~200-230 ms of serialized host link per preemption event, competing with the TP2 allreduce fallback path; and single recompute of a 22K request costs seconds of prefill (~7-15 s at plausible 1.5-3K tok/s 27B TP2 prefill [uncertain: prefill_rate_estimate]) plus a full 48-layer GDN state rebuild - both are catastrophic when the scheduler thrashes (the #47549 0.8-1.1 tok/s regime is preempt-recompute-repreempt livelock, not one event). (c) NVLink peer access (43.7 GB/s measured, plan/0004) makes a peer-GPU KV stash ~3.4x cheaper than host swap (~64 ms for the same 22K round trip) and is the only swap-like lever this hardware is good at - but no upstream code path exists, and under TP=2 the two ranks hold symmetric KV so the peer has no spare capacity by construction; it is only attractive in the 2-instance / shard topologies. VERDICT: run RECOMPUTE and treat any preemption event as a gate failure - the decision variable is the KV envelope and admission control (--max-num-seqs capped to the envelope minus >=20% watermark headroom; int8 KV as the default 22K+ arm), with the NVLink peer-stash recorded as a fork-level escape hatch (engine surgery, not configuration) should a swap-like path ever be justified. PROBE (assert engaged backend + KV dtype at load): boot each arm, parse the startup log - (1) attention-backend selection strings per layer group must show the intended backend for every full-attn layer (fork: BRIDGE_ATTN at d256; any TRITON_ATTN fallback string while a quantized KV dtype is requested = hard fail, that is exactly #47549 link 1-2 caught at t=0 at zero cost), (2) reconcile the reported 'GPU KV cache size: N tokens' against N_expected = floor(KV_budget / bytes_per_token[dtype]) - a ~2x shortfall or an exact match to the fp16 row while int8/K8V4 was requested = silent-fallback fail, (3) assert the GDN state pool size equals max_num_seqs x 144 MiB in the allocator report, (4) assert vllm:cache_config_info labels carry the requested kv dtype. Numerics before timing: PPL 2k must hold the 6.7761 +/- 0.0002 band and distinct3 logprobs the plan/0007 envelope per KV arm, plus a logprob-delta distribution vs fp16 KV per context bucket, plus - mandatory for any compressed-KV x MTP arm - a fixed-prompt temp-0 canary with a 4-gram repetition-ratio check (the #53180 detector: it passes smoke suites while corrupting traffic).
lacuna.upstream_base: Dated ledger for this surface: 2025-11-05 PyTorch blog 'Hybrid models as first-class citizens in vLLM' - V1 unified KV+Mamba allocator, page-size alignment, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE CUDA graphs; the V0 hybrid path (separate max_num_seqs-sized Mamba tensors) is the deprecated baseline. V1 preemption semantics settled by then: RECOMPUTE default, SWAP V0-only (#18115, 2025 era), swap metrics deprecated in the metrics design doc. 2026-04-17 #40094 - TurboQuant kv-cache-dtype presets present in mainline but rejected by TRITON_ATTN/FLASH_ATTN (backend-dtype coupling broken, open, unmaintained). 2026-04-24 #40831 - TurboQuant x MTP degenerate loops on Qwen3.6-27B hybrid; closed out-of-tree (genesis-vllm-patches P64-P69), NOT fixed upstream - treat upstream mainline as still carrying the bug. 2026-05-11 vllm.ai TurboQuant study blog - official comparison vs BF16/FP8 on long-context/reasoning workloads (4-bit favored there). 2026-07-03 #47549 - v0.24.0 drops FlashInfer from SM7.5 candidates; the last-good upstream base for quantized KV on sm75 is v0.23.0 (software FP8 KV via flashinfer-python 0.6.12); open, no maintainer response [uncertain: vllm_v023_v024_release_dates]. 2026-08-21 #53180 - bug family recurs on stock v0.27.1 (k8v4 + MTP-3, hybrid GDN, silent), proving the out-of-tree closure did not generalize. Fork positioning: the engine lane stays on the retained-Turing fork (v0.21.0-class); this item needs no upstream code - the envelope is arithmetic and the assertions are log/metric parsing - but every month of #47549/#40094/#53180 staying open strengthens the case that quantized-KV-on-sm75 is fork-resident permanently.

effort_value.effort_estimate: Small campaign, no kernel work: (a) envelope table as a committed artifact - pure geometry arithmetic plus the startup-log reconciliation harness (bytes/token by dtype, tokens/GiB, 22K/256K context costs, GDN state per-seq pricing, capacity on the 26-30 GiB budget), 0.5-1 day; (b) load-assertion probe - backend-selection strings, GPU-KV-cache-size reconciliation, state-pool size, cache_config_info dtype labels, hard-fail on silent fallback, 1 day including wiring into the plan/0007 gate harness; (c) zero-preemption admission sweep - operator shape (1x 22-32K session + small concurrent batch), find the --max-num-seqs boundary per KV arm where PREEMPTED events are zero and vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc stays under ~0.8, 1 day; (d) numerics per compressed-KV arm - logprob-delta vs fp16 KV plus the temp-0 canary with 4-gram repetition ratio for any x MTP arm, 1-2 days reusing the plan/0007 harness; (e) short design note recording the recompute+admission-control decision and the NVLink peer-stash as the deferred fork lever, 0.5 day. Total ~4-5 days single-operator; the sibling items (fp8-kv-and-activations, both-card-tp-nvlink-serving) then consume the table directly.
effort_value.unlocks: Makes capacity a first-class, checkable design variable instead of an implicit one: the stage-13 both-card campaign gets its admission limits and KV-dtype defaults from the table instead of discovering them as preemption storms; native 256K serving on 48 GB becomes an arithmetic claim (16 GiB fp16 / 8 GiB int8 / 6 GiB K8V4 per 256K context on the 27B hybrid) with a gate that proves it; the MTP-vs-TurboQuant conflict (#40831/#53180) is converted from a silent-corruption hazard into an explicit either/or row (fp16/int8 + MTP3 vs K8V4 without MTP) decided by measured acceptance rates; the 35B MoE secondary gets its own envelope row (native 256K needs int8 KV: 12 of 26-30 GiB); every future long-context agentic deployment (the RooCode/#47549 workload class) inherits a zero-preemption gate; and the load-time backend+dtype assertion closes the #47549 failure chain at link 1 on any rebase or upgrade, permanently.
effort_value.dependency_order: Landed already: the 27B TP=2 engine gate with PPL anchor 6.7761 (plan/0007, 2026-09-06), the W4A16 weights lane (14-15 GB), BRIDGE_ATTN owning d256, NVLink measured 43.7 GB/s (plan/0004), the tp2 variance/median-of-5 discipline (MEMORY 2026-09-07). This item needs only those and can start immediately; nothing else must land first. It feeds three siblings: both-card-tp-nvlink-serving (its probe step 2-3 IS this item's assertion set), fp8-kv-and-activations (the int8/fp8/K8V4 KV quality gate rides the same harness), and spec-decode-on-sm75 (the MTP x compressed-KV interaction matrix is one of its acceptance rows). External prerequisites: none for fp16 arms; int8-KV and TurboQuant arms depend on the dtype actually engaging on the fork engine (asserted by the probe, else the fp8-kv sibling's fork path must land first). Parallelizable: the envelope table and load-assertion harness are independent of the tp2 lockstep bisect and of all kernel lanes.
effort_value.risk_notes: (1) The silent-fallback trap is the whole point: on upstream, a quantized KV dtype request either hard-errors (TRITON_ATTN rejects fp8, #47549) or silently degrades (#53180-style green health with corrupted traffic) - an assertion that reads only exit codes proves nothing; the probe must parse the engaged backend, the token count, and the dtype label, and must canary-generate under any compressed-KV x MTP arm. (2) TurboQuant x MTP is field-broken on the exact model class (#40831 closed out-of-tree; #53180 open on v0.27.1 with PR #51812 ruled out) - do not ship K8V4+MTP3 (the weicj flagship preset) without an independent canary pass; fp8_e5m2+MTP is the only verified compressed combination, and fp8 KV itself needs the FlashInfer software path (<= v0.23.0-class or fork). (3) int8-KV-under-MTP is untested anywhere found - treat as unverified until the interaction probe runs. (4) Numerics: KV quantization is per-token/head rounding - accept on logprob-delta distributions vs fp16 KV per context bucket, not PPL alone; the PPL anchor (6.7761 +/- 0.0002) applies to the fp16 arm and must not be silently reused as the quantized-arm band. (5) GDN state pricing (144 MiB/seq) can invert expectations: token capacity that looks ample for 300 concurrent sequences is actually state-capped near 100-180; also the fp16-state (72 MiB) variant is a numerics change, not a free win. (6) Preemption behavior under the hybrid allocator: V1 supports preempting mamba hybrids by full recompute (state rebuild), mamba prefix caching is experimental (#26201) and was never tested with MTP (#39809), external offload is unsupported for hybrids (#38230) - so no upstream relief valve exists if the envelope is mis-sized; overflow goes straight to the #47549 livelock regime. (7) Upstream drift: v0.24.0+ has no sm75 quantized-KV backend at all; every month open (#47549, #40094, #53180) entrenches fork-resident solutions. (8) Metric-surface drift: preemption visibility moved from Prometheus gauges to PREEMPTED engine-core events in current V1 [uncertain: preempted_metric_surface] - pin the probe to whatever the fork base actually emits, assert on the scheduler-side counter.
effort_value.determinism_class: Layered. Bitwise-clean: the envelope arithmetic itself, the bytes/token constants (integer geometry), and the load-time reconciliation (deterministic allocator sizing for a fixed config - restart-to-restart stable unless NCCL/allocator nondeterminism shifts the overhead slice; the assertion needs a tolerance band, not exact equality). Statistical: KV-quantization quality (per-token/head rounding) - gate on a logprob-delta distribution vs fp16 KV, median over N sequences per context bucket; MTP acceptance rates - statistical quantities needing median-of-N; and the admission boundary (zero-preemption --max-num-seqs threshold) - it depends on arrival order, prefix-cache state, and GDN state occupancy, so the recorded boundary is the conservative edge of N repeated sweeps at fixed seeds, not a single number. Preemption itself is deterministic for a fixed schedule (FCFS + fixed arrivals) but any arrival-order perturbation distributes it - which is exactly why the gate is 'zero events under the operator shape', a predicate, not a rate. Constraint to hold: recompute-preemption changes batch shapes and triggers CUDA-graph re-record/piecewise selection on the hybrid path, and the split-K WS-zero-between-replays requirement (sibling item) means a preempted-then-restarted sequence must still land in the PPL/logprob bands - if a preemption event is ever observed during a numerics run, that run is void, not averaged.

decision.priority_signal: For doing this next: it is the cheapest item in the lacunae set (days, no kernels) while being the one that converts three known-silent failure modes (#47549 silent capacity loss, #40094 silent dtype rejection, #53180 silent corruption) into load-time hard failures; the stage-13 campaign cannot set --max-num-seqs, pick a KV dtype for 22K+, or choose between MTP3 and TurboQuant without this table, so it blocks the operator's own acceptance run; the failure chain is field-proven on the operator's exact workload class (agentic 18-24K contexts) and hardware class (SM7.5) by an 18-GPU fleet; and the #53180 recurrence (2026-08-21, stock v0.27.1) shows the ecosystem is not converging on fixes - the window where 'trust the engine defaults' is viable is closed, which raises the value of explicit gates. Against: the arithmetic portion is genuinely trivial and could be folded into the both-card campaign as a work package rather than standing alone; the probe adds gates but no capability. Window-closing: no upstream fix movement on any of the three issues. Verdict: do immediately and first among the ecosystem-strategy items - it is the prerequisite gate-set for both-card-tp-nvlink-serving, and its cost is a few days against months of mispriced capacity decisions.
decision.recommended_probe: Gate-0 style, oracle-first, no timing until numerics pass. ARM SET: fp16, int8, K8V4 (K8V4 run both with and without MTP3; fp16/int8 arms with MTP3). [uncertain: qwen36_27b_config_provenance - geometry inherited from this run's verified supplementation context and the sibling item's HF fetch, not independently re-fetched; moe_35b_geometry - the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B hybrid secondary named in #53180 has unverified geometry, only Qwen3-30B-A3B was confirmed this run.] STEP 1 (load assertion, zero-cost, the deliverable's core): boot Qwen3.6-27B-AutoRound TP=2 per arm; parse the startup transcript; assert (a) the attention-backend selection string per layer group is the intended backend on every rank (TRITON_ATTN appearing while a quantized KV dtype is requested = hard fail, the #47549 link caught at t=0), (b) reported 'GPU KV cache size: N tokens' reconciles with floor(KV_budget / bytes_per_token) for the REQUESTED dtype within the watermark tolerance (a match to the fp16 row = silent fallback, hard fail), (c) GDN state pool = max_num_seqs x 144 MiB, (d) cache_config_info carries the requested dtype. STEP 2 (envelope confirmation): for each arm record N tokens and compute the 22K-session concurrency the table predicts; sweep --max-num-seqs across the predicted boundary. STEP 3 (zero-preemption predicate): run the operator shape - one 22-32K context request with prefix caching plus the small concurrent batch - per arm and per --max-num-seqs value; assert zero PREEMPTED engine events (scheduler-side counter) with kv_cache_usage_perc < ~0.8 throughout; record the zero-preemption admission boundary per dtype into the committed envelope table. STEP 4 (numerics): fp16 arm must hold PPL 2k = 6.7761 +/- 0.0002 and the plan/0007 distinct3 logprob envelope at ctx 512/2048/8192/16384/32768; each quantized-KV arm gates on the logprob-delta distribution vs the fp16 arm (median over N sequences per bucket); each compressed-KV x MTP arm additionally runs the fixed-prompt temp-0 canary with a 4-gram repetition-ratio threshold (the #53180 detector - expect K8V4+MTP to FAIL this, which is the intended, decisive outcome). STEP 5 (only then timing): median-of-5 across >= 3 engine restarts per surviving arm. Kill-switch logic: if int8 KV cannot engage on the fork engine (STEP 1b fails), the 22K+ envelope collapses 2x and the fp8-kv-and-activations sibling becomes the blocking dependency before stage 13; if K8V4+MTP fails the canary (expected per #53180), the decision row is settled - K8V4 is the no-speculation long-context arm and MTP3 rides the fp16/int8 arms - and no further investigation is warranted on this hardware until upstream or the fork patches the draft-head/cache interaction.
